0.0.n: Sets the time for the video introduction.

0.1.n: Marks today as the topic being introduced.

0.2.n: Comes before a noun to ask about its type.

0.3.n: The speaker is introducing the video viewers are watching.

0.4.n: Marks どんな動画 as a question embedded within the sentence.

0.5.n: Links the preceding question to 言います, marking what is being said.

0.6.n: The polite form of 言う, used here to introduce an explanation.

0.7.n: Makes かと言いますと an introductory phrase like if you ask what it is.

1.1.n: Part of the TV program name 旅サラダ, not a separate trip here.

1.2.n: Completes the TV program name 旅サラダ; it does not refer to food here.

1.4.n: Added to the program name to show respect toward the show and its team.

1.5.n: Marks the program as the context in which the location filming took place.

1.6.n: A place name identifying where the filming took place.

1.7.n: Connects Kyoto to ロケ, specifying the location of the shoot.

1.8.n: A shortened borrowed word used for filming outside a studio.

1.9.n: Marks ロケ as the activity the speaker was allowed to do.

1.10.n: Past humble form of させていただく, presenting the activity as something others kindly allowed the speaker to do.

1.11.n: Follows the past verb phrase to identify the occasion being discussed.

1.12.n: Marks とき as the time when the following filming happened.

2.0.n: Modifies 裏側, suggesting modest, casual glimpses rather than extensive coverage.

2.1.n: Literally the back side, used here for moments outside the main production.

2.2.n: Casually presents behind-the-scenes moments as examples, without making the description sound exact.

2.3.n: Marks the setting where the speaker filmed.

2.4.n: Used with 回す to describe recording video.

2.5.n: Marks カメラ as what the speaker operated.

2.6.n: Past form of 回す; カメラを回す means to run the camera, not physically rotate it.

2.7.n: Gives the reason for the compilation described in the next line.

2.9.n: Points back to the behind-the-scenes moments just mentioned.

2.10.n: Refers to what those moments looked like, as captured on camera.

2.11.n: Marks その様子 as what gets compiled in the next line.

3.0.n: やって is the linking form of やる; みたかった adds wanted to try.

3.1.n: 風 attaches to Vlog to mean in the style of a vlog.

3.2.n: Marks the style the footage was arranged into.

3.3.n: Polite past form of まとめる, describing compiling the recorded scenes.

3.4.n: Connects the completed compilation to the invitation that follows.

3.6.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request to enjoy the video.

4.0.n: Politely addresses all the viewers directly.

4.2.n: Combines with に to describe sharing the imagined trip with the speaker.

4.3.n: Completes 一緒に, making it describe how the traveling happens.

4.4.n: A place name identifying the area viewers are invited to imagine exploring.

4.5.n: Marks Kyoto as the area traveled through, rather than a destination reached.

4.6.n: Casual shortening of 旅している; dropping い is common in speech.

4.7.n: The preceding phrase describes the feeling: traveling through Kyoto together.

4.8.n: Marks the mindset in which viewers should enjoy the video.

4.9.n: The linking form 楽しんで plus ください makes a polite request.

0.lit: As for today, if I say what kind of video it is,
0.tip: かと言いますと introduces an explanation, rather than asking viewers to answer a question.

1.lit: When I had the opportunity to do a Kyoto location shoot for Tabi Salad,
1.tip: させていただいた humbly presents doing the shoot as an opportunity granted by others.

2.lit: Because I ran the camera in little behind-the-scenes moments and such, those scenes,
2.tip: カメラを回す means to film; the final を connects その様子 to the next line's verb.

3.lit: I put together in a vlog style I had wanted to try, so, by all means,
3.tip: やってみたかった combines trying something with having wanted to do it.

4.lit: Everyone, please enjoy with the feeling that you are traveling through Kyoto together!
4.tip: 旅してる気分で invites viewers to enjoy the video as if they were traveling along.
